messages:
maya: Thinking through a simpler default for canary pacing on model swaps. Current step lists are huge and folks keep getting it wrong. Proposal: a compact, signal-driven phased pacer with built-in holdpoints.

raj: +1 to simpler. can you sketch the actual stages? e.g. tiny -> small -> fast -> ramp?

maya: yea — something like: 0.1% (sanity), 1% (small cohort), 5% (functional), 25% (load), 100% (cutover). each stage has a configurable duration and a guard set (latency, error-rate, eval-drift).

casey: we need to define numeric guard gates. p50/p95 latency delta, 5xx rate, and eval-quality regression on a small prompt set. also cost-per-token shouldn't jump > X%.

raj: suggestion: gates = {p50_delta_ms: 100, p95_delta_ms: 250, error_rate_pct: 0.5, eval_regression_pct: 1.0, cost_pct: 15}. keep them permissive by default but exposed in API.

maya: agreed. also want a "safety_hold" flag per stage that forces manual confirmation before proceeding. default for the first two stages = false, for 5%+ = true.

casey: how will console show this? UX needs a compact timeline, stage timers, and "pause & inspect" button. plus quick links to telemetry (latency heatmap, error traces, eval diffs).

maya: exact. console should show real-time stage pass/fail, and the reason for any automated rollback. e.g. "rollback triggered: p95 latency +380ms over baseline".

raj: API shape idea — keep it small and composable. e.g.:

```yaml
rollout: 
  type: canary
  stages:
    - pct: 0.1
      duration_min: 10
      guards: {p50_ms: 200, error_pct: 1.0}
    - pct: 1
      duration_min: 20
      guards: {p50_ms: 150, error_pct: 0.8}
    - pct: 5
      duration_min: 30
      safety_hold: true
      guards: {p95_ms: 250, error_pct: 0.5, eval_regression_pct: 1.0}
    - pct: 25
      duration_min: 60
      safety_hold: true
      guards: {p95_ms: 300, error_pct: 0.3}
    - pct: 100
      duration_min: 5
      final: true
```

taylor: small nit: use pct as integer or float? we should be consistent with routing layer which expects float (0-1) in some places. normalize on integers (0-100) in API for readability, convert internally.

maya: good catch. use integers in API. internal components keep float. we'll document conversion.

casey: what about cohort targeting? some customers want percent + key-slice (e.g., 10% traffic but only new users). we should support an optional "selector" per stage: e.g. "cohort: new-user=true" or by region.

raj: add a sticky-routing option — some apps require session stickiness so a user in the canary stays in it for subsequent requests. default = true for user_id keyed selectors, false otherwise.

maya: telemetry hooks: sample 1% of requests for full text evaluation payload (not just logs), attach to eval-harness, run lightweight quality checks (embedding drift, hallucination signals) and surface regression score. if regression score > threshold -> fail stage.

casey: agree but call out privacy constraints. only sample if customer has allowed sampling (opt-in) and we mask PII before forwarding to eval.

maya: noted. add a required flag sample_e2e: {enabled: bool, retention_days: int} and a consent check.

deploy-bot: canary start: model=rw-model-v2->v3, rollout=2278901234, stage=0.1%, started at 2278901234

raj: example automated rollback rule: if (error_pct > guard.error_pct) OR (p95_delta > guard.p95_ms) OR (eval_regression_pct > guard.eval_regression_pct) then rollback to previous stable. also schedule a slack alert + incident channel post.

maya: yes. and add "soft-threshold" alarms (warning, but still continue unless hard-threshold breached). warnings should create a pinned item in the console timeline for triage.

taylor: edge cases: very low-traffic customers — 0.1% may not be meaningful. we should support absolute-min-requests-per-stage or a time-window fallback that extends duration until N requests seen. e.g., min_requests: 1000 or max_wait_minutes: 720.

maya: good. default min_requests = 500 for production tiers, 50 for dev.

casey: one more: quota interaction. if customer-level quota or reserved capacity is hit during mid-roll, stage should either pause or move to fallback model (lighter quantized variant). we need explicit policy: "on_quota_exhaust: pause | fallback | continue(raise)".

maya: include that. default = pause + notify.

e2e-bot: e2e: scheduled a canary-smoke test run at stage 1% and 5% for rollout 2278901234. tests: basic prompts, rate-limited burst, token-cost check.

raj: next steps: i'll draft the API proto and a concise console mockup. maya — can you write the default guard table and min/timeout heuristics? casey/taylor: can you validate telemetry hooks and sampling/privacy text for docs?

maya: will do. aiming for a PR with config schema + console mock by EOD Thu.

casey: I'll sketch the dashboard tiles and the pause/inspect UX tomorrow.

taylor: I'll audit routing layer for integer pct support and sticky behavior.

maya: thanks all. we'll iterate after the PR.
